chunks: And Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Muʿattib, from Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:

"Go and give zakat al-fitrah on behalf of our household and for the servants, and include them all, and do not leave any one of them out; for if you leave out a person from them, I fear for him al-fawt."

key_terms.الرَّقِيقِ: the servants or slaves under one's care
key_terms.الْفَوْتَ: loss or missing out, explained here as death
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةَ: zakat al-fitrah, the alms due at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about giving zakat al-fitrah for every member of the household?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs that zakat al-fitrah must be given on behalf of all members of one's household, including servants, without leaving anyone out. It emphasizes the seriousness of this duty by warning of "al-fawt," which the Imam عليه السلام explains as death.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2078 - It is narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Mu’attib, who said:
Abu Abdullah (as) said:
"Go and give Zakat al-Fitr on behalf of our household and for the servants. Include all of them and do not leave anyone out. If you leave out even one person, I fear for them the 'fawt' (loss)."
